source_span: we remain of the view that next week's CPI will be a critical catalyst to watch compared to today's NFP, given that wage inflation has not been the driving force for inflation and Warsh's assessment of labor market productivity
source_chain: Waller's dovish comments (inflation cooling, he'd support a hold) cut priced September hike odds to 51% from 63% therefore bonds/stocks rallied Thursday; but ISM services prices-paid hit a four-year high of 72.6, pushing the 12-month average to 68.5 (highest since April 2023) and this series leads CPI by 2-3 months, therefore the disinflation Waller cited is unconfirmed; therefore JPM does not expect Friday's NFP to settle the debate at all and holds that CPI on Sep 11 is the actual decisive catalyst, with the Fed holding only if core CPI prints +0.1% to +0.2% MoM and payrolls land near 50k. Invalidation: a hot Sep 11 core CPI print, not the NFP number itself.
pulse_chain: August NFP printed 162,000, blowing past every bank's forecast (JPM 50k, DB 65k, GS 40k, Street 55k) therefore the dovish case built on Waller's comments (which rested on a cooling labor market) is killed; combined with ISM prices-paid at a four-year high, therefore the market has repriced toward a hawkish Fed (front-end yields up, 2yr at a post-Jan-2025 high). JPM's actual view that CPI decides the meeting rather than NFP is recast as a secondary 'counter' that 'cuts less than it looks,' subordinate to an NFP-driven narrative. Invalidation given: Sep 11 core CPI at +0.1% to +0.2% keeps the hold alive.
why: No source document contains an actual August NFP print (all sourced notes, including the same day's JPM briefing and Deutsche Bank's Reid note, predate the 8:30am release and only forecast it, as the shadow pulse drafted from the identical source set correctly reflects), and the pulse inverts JPM's actually-argued mechanism — that NFP 'does not mean much' and CPI is the decisive catalyst — into a subordinate counter-argument beneath an NFP-driven collapse narrative the source never makes.
